children: Virtus Diversified Income & Convertible Fund will raise its monthly distribution to $0.215 from $0.18 starting with the October payment, about a 19% increase. The new rate equals ~10.1% of market price ($25.63) and ~9.7% of NAV ($26.69) as of Sep. 22, 2026.
Higher cash yield can narrow the market discount and attract income-focused buyers.
Magnitude signals confidence in cash generation or a plan to address the NAV discount.
Headline yield screens high for retail income traders; can drive demand.
Indicates payout level versus portfolio earning power; informs sustainability.
Portion may be ROC if income/gains shortfall; payout not a performance proxy.

This is a tactical step to boost distribution attractiveness and address a market discount, consistent with closed-end fund practices. For a larger catalyst, watch if the market discount to NAV tightens and if payouts are covered by income/gains rather than return of capital.
